ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, Ultimate Beneficial Owners and proposed senior managers against: (i) OFAC SDN List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Spanish Ministry of Economy and Digital Transformation / SEPBLAC restrictive measures; and (v) national PEP databases. A risk-based Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered by PEP status, high-risk jurisdictions, or unusual transaction patterns. Screening must be documented and retained for at least ten years under Ley 10/2010.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Servicio de Certificación de Denominaciones Sociales; online access via the official notary/registrar network (www.registradores.org / www.rmc.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name may be in Spanish or in any co-official Spanish language, and foreign-language names must use the Latin alphabet with Spanish transliteration. All official corporate filings and the articles of association must be prepared in Spanish. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Spanish or EU-registered company name, and must not contravene public order, morals, or mandatory legal provisions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name certificates are non-transferable and cannot be extended; if the 90-day validity lapses, a fresh application must be filed. Upon rejection, the applicant or notary may submit a written request for re-examination to the Registro Mercantil Central within 20 business days. If the rejection is confirmed, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (currently Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública) at the Ministry of Justice. Further judicial review is available before the Spanish administrative courts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used for administrative correspondence and as a commercial address, and is generally acceptable for a low-risk LegalTech SaaS company, provided that the registered office (domicilio social) is a physical, contactable address in Spain at which the directors or legal representative can receive service of process. A mere PO Box or sub-address without any managed presence is not compliant. The commercial registry and tax administration expect at least minimal physical substance such as staff, servers/equipment, or contractual office services to support non-resident ownership.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk. For a standard non-licensed LegalTech SaaS entity with no statutory license, no cash heavy activity, and payment rails limited to Stripe/cards, the probability of an unannounced physical inspection is estimated at 2–5% per year during the initial post-incorporation period. This risk increases to 15–25% if suspicious transaction reports, tax audit triggers, frequent UBO changes, or high-risk jurisdictional links arise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC); applicable sections include Articles 20 (public deed), 21 (registration), 22 (incorporation), 73-84 (S.L. capital structure), 102-116 (registered office), 124-131 (administrators), and 209-236 (first board organization).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central and the corresponding Registro Mercantil Provincial; pre-incorporation endowment certification through the Colegio Notarial or a Spanish credit institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public incorporation deed) filed with the competent Registro Mercantil Provincial, preceded by certification of the company name from the Registro Mercantil Central.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: S.L. minimum capital is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,270), which must be fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind at incorporation; the capital must be deposited in escrow with a Spanish credit institution or evidenced by notarial certification of the contribution before the public deed is granted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the shares representing 100% of the subscribed capital be provisionally allotted to the founding members in accordance with the deed of incorporation, subject to definitive registration in the book of registered partners. (2) That the registered office of the Company be fixed and adopted at the address stated in Article [X] of the bylaws, and that the managing director be authorized to execute the lease or title documentation and to notify all competent registries and tax authorities. (3) That [Name] be appointed sole Administrator and that [Name] be appointed Secretary of the corporate records, each accepting their office. (4) That the Administrator be granted the broadest powers to open bank accounts, appoint agents, and complete any further filings required to register the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate from the Central Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (with collaboration of the Registro Mercantil Provincial or online through the official 'NO MERCANTIL' service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application through the Registro Mercantil Central portal or in-person at any Registro Mercantil Provincial, providing up to six proposed S.L. names in order of preference. Deposit the statutory fee and wait for the certificación negativa de denominación (negative name certificate), which confirms no identical or confusingly similar company name exists. The name certificate is valid for three months and must be attached to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Duly completed name request form (solicitud de certificación)
Copy of the applicant’s official ID (DNI/NIE/passport)
Payment proof of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a requested name is rejected for similarity, revise the denomination list and resubmit immediately; the registry will hold priority rights for a re-filed application within 30 days. If the certificate expires before the deed is granted, obtain a new certificate without any penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Deposit Escrow Account and Obtain Contribution Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank or savings bank) where the escrow account is opened; alternatively, a notary certifies that the capital is fully paid before the deed signature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account in the proposed S.L. name with at least EUR 3,000 deposited. The bank issues a deposit certificate (certificado de depósito de capital) stating the account holder, amount deposited, and express limitation that funds cannot be disposed of until the certificate is cancelled after registration. For in-kind contributions, obtain a notarial valuation report attached to the deed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate
Preliminary draft of the articles of association showing the proposed corporate name
Bank account opening forms and AML/KYC documentation (passport, proof of address, corporate background information)
Draft list of shareholders and their respective contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account due to incomplete KYC, cure the file by providing notarized powers of attorney for each non-resident director/shareholder and updated utility bills or bank references. If capital is held for more than two months, renew the bank certificate; banks may charge a small maintenance fee which is a recoverable corporate expense.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Grant the Public Incorporation Deed before a Spanish Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the proposed registered office; typically any notary in Spain may authorize the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the chosen notary with the negative name certificate, deposit certificate, company bylaws (estatutos), draft deed, and identification of all founding members (whether individuals or legal entities). If there are corporate shareholders, present constitutive documents, powers of attorney, and evidence of the resolution to incorporate. The notary verifies the legal capacity, capital contribution, and legality of the bylaws. The notary drafts and notarizes the escriitura de constitución and issues authenticated first copies for recording in the Commercial Registry, Tax Agency (AEAT), and Social Security (TGSS).
required_dossiers: Certificate of negative name from the Registro Mercantil Central
Bank deposit certificate for the EUR 3,000 minimum capital
Full identification documents of each founding shareholder
Notarial valuation report for any in-kind contributions
Draft articles of association (estatutos) signed by all founders
If a corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation, articles, directors’ resolution, and notarized power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects (defectos subsanables), the founders execute a written amendment (subsanación) to the draft deed, re-appear, and the notary re-grants the deed. If the defect relates to capital valuation, a new independent expert valuation must be obtained prior to re-signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), local tax administration office (Administración de la Agencia Tributaria) matching the registered office address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (Declaración censal) together with the attested copy of the public deed and the first authenticated copy (copia autorizada) or notary's certification that the deed was granted. The AEAT registers the company in the census and issues a provisional CIF/NIF (now legal entity ID, NIF, with letter 'S' for provisional). This provisional NIF is used for tax payments, invoicing, and before start of business activity. Within one month after registration in the Commercial Registry, must apply for the definitive NIF certificate by filing the official registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Form 036 (duly completed with the activity code ISIC 6201 / CNAE 6201)
Copia autorizada (notarized first copy) of the incorporation deed
Power of attorney of the tax representative if applicable
DNI/NIE of the legal representative
Spanish bank account details for tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT queries the activity code or management address, respond through the electronic office within 10 business days with a corrected Form 036 and lease/ownership evidence of the registered office. If the provisional NIF is not issued, escalate to the AEAT taxpayer assistance service and re-submit in person; a delay beyond 15 days may be appealed as a deemed denial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company in the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial corresponding to the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the execution of the incorporation deed, file the first copy of the deed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial. The registry verifies the legal validity of the deed, the identity and capacity of the founders, the minimum capital deposit, the legal form, and the legality of the articles. Once the registration (inscripción) is granted, the company acquires full legal personality and the registration is published in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil) and the Spanish Official Gazette. The registry may also issue a certified copy of the registration certificate to obtain the definitive NIF.
required_dossiers: First notarial copy (copia autorizada) of the public incorporation deed
Completed application form from the official registry model
Evidence of payment of the registration fee (if not paid via the notary’s integrated system)
DNI/NIE of the designated administrator
Certificate of the subscribed and paid capital in escrow (or cancellation copy after notification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect note (nota de defectos), the administrator or the notary submits the required additional documents within the statutory 60-day cure period. If the registration is denied through a motivated resolution, appeal within one month through the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública. All direct fees and notary fees are maintained at official tariffs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Definitive NIF and Activate Tax Census (Form 036) and Electronic ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Registro de Identificación Fiscal de Personas Jurídicas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the Commercial Registry registration certificate, submit Form 036 application for the definitive NIF. Attach the registry certification (certificado de registro) and the copy of the deed already registered. The AEAT converts the provisional NIF (S) into the definitive NIF and issues the definitive certificate (cédula de identificación fiscal). The company must also apply for the digital certificate (certificado electrónico) of the legal representative to use electronic AEAT services and, if the company expects to file VAT or income tax returns, register for the mandatory electronic mailbox (Dirección Electrónica Habilitada - DEH) for Tax Agency communications.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry registration certificate
Copy of the public deed showing the registered date and registration page
Form 036 (updates of any previous provisional filing)
Legal representative’s DNI/NIE and digital certificate application
Notarized authorization for tax representation if sending a gestor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF application is delayed due to pending proof of effective office, submit the lease contract and utility deposit to the AEAT. For electronic certificate issues, schedule an AEAT office appointment to obtain the certificate in person or use the cloud signature service with the registered administrator’s ID.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company and Directors for Social Security (TGSS) and Work-related Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) — provincial administration where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the standard incorporation forms (partes de inscripción) with the TGSS to register the employer (inscripción de empresa) and obtain a Código de Cuenta de Cotización for each work center. Register the sole administrator/director as a director-company official under the applicable special regime or, if there is an employment relationship, register the employees under the general social security regime. The TGSS will authorize a remote number (RED system) for electronic payroll submissions. Obtain proof of start-of-work-center notification (comunicación de apertura) if the company physically occupies premises.
required_dossiers: Company NIF certificate and deed of incorporation
Commercial Registry registration certificate
Legal representative’s ID and TGSS powers
List of administrators and their NIF/DNI
Proof of registered office lease or ownership
Corporate appointment deeds or board minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS rejects the registration due to missing activity classification, correct the CNAE 6201 code from the deed or the statistical activity declaration, and resubmit. If the administrator does not fall under the appropriate regime (social security), request a binding TGSS classification ruling before the business start.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Start-of-Business Declaration with the Municipal Licensing Department and Obtain N.I.E./Activities Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento (City Council) of the municipality of the registered office; plus the AEAT for the IAE (Impuesto sobre Actividades Económicas) filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the declaración de inicio de actividad with the local City Council, listing the intended activity under the municipal fee (tasa) and, if the company is non-exempt, apply for the IAE registration under Group 620 (informática and similar). For the cloud LegalTech activity, no industrial license is required under provincial regulations; however, if the company elects to operate from designated rented spaces, provide proof of planning/ownership compatibility. For IAE, large taxpayers and certain limited companies are exempt for the first two years, but they must nevertheless file this activity start declaration. The result of the municipal licensing procedure may be subject to a simple profession-compatible certificate (declaración responsable) rather than a full license.
required_dossiers: Company NIF and Commercial Registry certificate
Form 036 (IAE and census section)
Lease or ownership title for the registered office
Municipal operating declaration or declaración responsable
Administrator appointment deed
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires an environmental activity license even for office-based SaaS, request a pre-vetting (consulta previa) to obtain a written resolution confirming exempt status. If the license is granted with conditions (e.g., accessibility or security upgrades), appeal to the local specialized administrative courts (Juzgado de lo Contencioso-Administrativo) within 2 months, or cure by adopting required technical measures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Company Bylaws in a Notarial Act and Record the First Board Resolution and Appointment of Statutory Auditor (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notarial incorporation deed already integrates the company bylaws; after registration, the board must hold its first meeting and adopt the pro-forma resolution to organize governance. For an SL, there is no statutory requirement to appoint an auditor unless for two consecutive years the company exceeds at least two of the three thresholds (Total assets EUR 2.85 million, net turnover EUR 5.7 million, or 50 average employees) in which case submit the appointment of the audit firm in the annual accounts. A first board resolution (provided above) may be executed in a private deed or notarial act, but if there is any change of administrators, the notarial instrument must be registered so that the Commercial Registry certifies the new appointment. Minute book protocols must be established, such as the Libro Registro de Socios and Libro de Actas.
required_dossiers: Copy of the registered incorporation deed
Pro-forma board minutes (as per the first resolution wording)
Individual signed appointments (nombramientos) of administrators/secretary
Blank share certificates or first issuance documentation
Draft corporate books registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry blocks registration of the administrator due to disqualification criteria, substitute the administrator by a new notarial agreement and register the replacement. If statutory auditor thresholds are met and no auditor is appointed, cure within 30 days by ordinary general meeting resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay the Provincial Capital Transfer Tax Stamp Duty (ITP/AJD) and Register the Deed in the Official Land Registry if Required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Tributaria de la Comunidad Autónoma (regional tax agency); alternatively, the official tax office of the Autonomous Community where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days from the execution of the incorporation deed, declare and pay the stamp duty for the incorporation of a new company under the AJD (Actos Jurídicos Documentados) modality. The applicable rate varies by Autonomous Community (typically 0.75% of the nominal value of the deed, excluding any contributions, but some Communities like Madrid may apply a zero rate to the incorporation of new companies; Cataluña may charge up to 1.5%). Submit Form 600 (Impuesto sobre Actos Jurídicos Documentados) to the regional authority in the registered office region, seating the deed in the corresponding tax office. If the incorporation deed transfers real estate rights or a business, the land registration and Transfer Tax (ITP) may additionally apply.
required_dossiers: First copy of the incorporation deed (copia autorizada)
Form 600 (declaration of AJD)
Bank proof of the paid tax
Certificate of the final number of shares/subscription and capital notarized in the deed
NIF of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional tax office recalculates the taxable base or requests supplementary documents, file an amicable appeal (recurso de reposición) within one month before the same body, or if defect relates to formal registration, pay the supplemental amount plus late-payment interest. If the incorrect form (600 vs 033) was used, request a rectification within the statutory voluntary period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria, Comercio y Consumo of the Autonomous Community (not applicable to cloud LegalTech SaaS; if a physical office/data center is present, Dirección General de Industria and municipal licensing may intervene; however, ISIC 6201 is non-industrial).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad (responsible start-of-activity declaration) before the Ayuntamiento; no separate industrial manufacturing permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and corresponding Comunidad Autónoma environmental authority (Consejería de Medio Ambiente)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Non-EIA (ISIC 6201 does not appear in Annex I or II of Ley 21/2013 de evaluación ambiental); no full EIA or environmental impact statement is required for a cloud technology service, unless installing physical data centers above 100 kW or handling hazardous waste, in which case a municipal environmental license and the regional EIA for energy infrastructure may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If physical office premises are equipped: compliance with RD 1027/2007 (RITE) for HVAC, maximum allowed sound pressure levels per RD 1367/2007 (e.g., 85 dB(A) in workplaces during maximum daily exposure), and municipal noise thresholds (typically ≤55 dB(A) daytime) for technical cooling. For any electronic equipment waste, comply with RD 110/2015 on WEEE: deliver to authorized manager, maintain waste documentation for five years; for wastewater discharges to municipal sewerage, if water use is solely sanitary, no special discharge permit is required, but if industrial washing or chemical containment occurs, adhere to municipal discharge limits for pH (6.5-9) and COD (≤500 mg/L, where applicable).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Emergency and self-protection plan (Plan de Autoprotección) must be filed and approved by the local civil protection or fire authority for a building containing the activity, when total occupancy exceeds 100 persons, or the lease provides that the landlord holds a valid fire certificate. Fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation signage must comply with RIPCI (RD 513/2017), and periodic inspections at least annually. Structural load inspections: the lessor/owner of commercial premises must produce an ITE (Technical Building Inspection) certificate or a building status report showing earthquake load and structural stability, and if the building is used as a public access office for clients, an accessibility certificate under CTE DB-SUA is required. Occupational clearance: through the Servicio de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales (SPRL), conduct a workplace risk assessment and deliver employee safety training for office work with computer screens (PVD per RD 488/1997); if the company contracts staff, documentation of the preventive measures must be kept in the company technical record (Técnico de Prevención) and presented to the ITSS labor inspectorate on demand. If no premises, only an electronically served business model is used, no physical clearance is needed, but a telegraphic civil-defense compliance proof is the attestation that no public interaction premises or hardware installations are present.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Madrid; electronic portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (Modelo 036/037 census registration, Modelo 200 CIT return, IVA electronic filing, SII and Veri*factu APIs).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish SL: obtain a provisional NIF (Modelo 036) immediately after the notarial deed, inscribe the entity in the Registro Mercantil, then obtain the definitive NIF (letter prefix 'B' for SL) from the AEAT and complete registration in the Censo de Empresarios. For a foreign non-resident entity providing LegalTech SaaS without a Spanish permanent establishment: obtain the non-resident NIF (prefix 'N') via Modelo 036 before invoicing Spanish customers, appoint a tax representative resident in Spain when required, and register for IVA using the same model where any taxable transaction arises in Spain; otherwise, the foreign entity requires only a foreign VAT ID and will be subject to Spanish reverse charge on inbound services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The SL is a tax-resident corporation fully subject to Spanish corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) at a general rate of 25%; newly incorporated SLs pay 15% on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable profit in the first two fiscal years (art. 29.1 LIS). Tax scope is worldwide income for resident entities, with no check-the-box pass-through; the common territorial regime (territorio común, with Madrid as the seat) applies to the entity. Local fiscal distinctions (foral regimes of País Vasco and Navarra) constitute a separate provincial exception outside the default unitary national classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Spain. Available statutory elections: (i) tax consolidation (Régimen de Consolidación Fiscal, art. 58 LIS) for a group head holding at least 75% directly or indirectly in subsidiaries; (ii) 100% participation exemption (art. 21 LIS) for foreign dividends and capital gains with a minimum 5% holding held for 12 months; (iii) ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) election for a Spanish holding company managing EU and non-EU participations; (iv) reduced 15% CIT rate election for newly created SLs for the first two taxable periods; (v) hybrid mismatch neutrality adjustments and elections under Law 11/2021 (ATAD transposition) for financial instruments and deductible payments; (vi) election between the foreign tax credit (art. 31 LIS) and the participation exemption where both apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), Spanish Value Added Tax, implemented under Ley 37/1992 and EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: any taxable person performing economic activity in Spain must register for IVA via Modelo 036/037 before commencing operations (art. 164 LIVA). For distance sales and OSS e-commerce supplies to Spanish consumers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies; no monetary threshold exists for intra-EU B2B reverse-charge services or for the establishment of a fixed establishment. Real-time SII reporting is mandatory when turnover exceeds EUR 6,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Yes - mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Ley 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece) and Real Decreto 1007/2023 (Veri*factu). Invoices must be generated by AEAT-certified software embedding a QR-code cryptographic hash that guarantees authenticity, integrity, readability and real-time traceability; issuers must transmit invoice records, rectifications and cancellations to the AEAT through API/web-service integration, while recipients must retain acceptance records. Large enterprises (turnover above EUR 6,000,000) file SII-IVA records within 4 business days for the Iberian Peninsula and 8 business days for the Canary Islands, Balearic Islands, Ceuta and Melilla. The Facturae XML format is mandatory in B2G public procurement; paper invoices are prohibited for public-sector transactions and may be disallowed as a business expense deduction for the recipient.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Spanish VAT law confers exemption with the right to deduct input VAT (export zero-rating). Exports of goods to third countries qualify under art. 21 LIVA upon documented exit of the goods from the EU customs territory. For the LegalTech SaaS and e-signature business model (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541199), supplies of cloud document automation, electronic signature authentication and digital storage services to customers established outside Spain are deemed rendered outside Spanish territory (art. 69.1.1º LIVA), and no Spanish IVA is chargeable where the customer provides its foreign VAT/GST identification number and the contract states the place-of-supply rule. B2C supplies of digital services to non-EU final consumers also fall outside the Spanish VAT scope under the destination principle. Unlike FX-control jurisdictions, Spanish law does not impose a statutory 180-day repatriation deadline for ordinary export receivables; the 180-day convention is used as a bank/audit reference for export financing and insurance recognition.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo), Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document, Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT credit advice)
Commercial invoice and packing list with Incoterms reference
Foreign client's tax-residence certificate and foreign VAT/GST identification number
Signed SaaS/e-signature service agreement containing the place-of-supply and VAT attribution clauses
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: High audit scrutiny under the AEAT annual Plan de Control Tributario and the IVA anti-fraud task force. Unjustified zero-rating/exemption claims trigger retrospective reassessment of the omitted IVA, late-payment interest from the original due date (art. 26 LGT), and an infringement penalty of 50% to 150% of the defrauded amount (art. 184 LGT), plus loss of the 'operador autorizado' / 'exportador autorizado' status. Documents falsified to support export exemption constitute the criminal offence of contrabando under Ley Orgánica 12/1995, punishable by fines of up to double the value of the goods or amount at stake and imprisonment of up to six years, extending to customs agents and tax representatives. Non-compliance with Veri*factu QR and transmission obligations is independently fined between EUR 150 and EUR 10,000 per invoice or omitted registration, without prejudice to VAT reassessment, clawback of refunds and publication on the tax-debtors' list.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting as the monetary authority and financial supervisor, together with the Dirección General de Transacciones Internacionales of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for balance-of-payments and foreign investment reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under a full liberalised capital and current account convertibility regime compliant with EU treaty freedoms and OECD codes. The euro is freely convertible within the eurozone; no prior exchange control authorisation is required for foreign direct investment, financing, or profit repatriation. Non-resident shareholders may remit dividends and liquidation proceeds freely after corporate tax and withholding clearances, but must satisfy Bank of Spain statistical declarations for balances exceeding €50,000 or for direct investment capital movements. Current account payments for SaaS licensing and contract-automation service fees are unrestricted, subject only to transfer pricing and anti-money-laundering verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender or forced conversion ratio applies in Spain. Spanish exporters and service providers are permitted to retain export proceeds in foreign currency or convert at freely negotiated market rates. Statutory balance-of-payments reporting obligations to the Banco de España require declaration of transactions exceeding €50,000 or where required by the foreign transaction form (Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior), but this is an information return, not a surrender requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for inbound EU SME treasury operations using SEPA and SWIFT rails. Spanish SLs may lawfully open payment accounts with EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), provided the EMI is authorised in an EEA state and registered with the Banco de España for cross-border pass-through. However, the EMI account will not constitute a domestic credit institution account for certain tax-facilitation purposes, and full treasury resilience requires a tier-one bank account. Offshore digital EMIs established outside the EU face low viability due to the absence of EEA licensing and Spanish regulatory rejection of their account-opening services for domestic operating entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not universally mandated in Spain, but is strongly preferred for non-resident shareholders and directors. In practice, tier-one banks require the Spanish SL's appointed director or a registered attorney-in-fact (apoderado) with formal notarial power to attend an in-person KYC interview at a Spanish branch. Remote video-identification is accepted by certain online banking channels for individual residents, but for a corporate legal entity with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners, physical presence or a notarised power of attorney issued before a Spanish consulate is the prevailing compliance standard. A majority of banks will reject fully remote corporate onboarding without an existing relationship or high-quality documentary lodgement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) unable to provide a Spanish tax identification number (NIE/NIF) and foreign tax number.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passport copies; NIE certificate or application receipt; foreign tax identification certificate; UBO declaration form under Spanish AML Law 10/2010; certificate of good standing from the registry of the UBO's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for share capital injection appears as a third-party transfer not linked to the contractual shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed share subscription agreement; notarised capital increase deed; bank SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's verified account; audited bank statements for the last 3 months; explanation memorandum on the commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 6201 SaaS activity deemed intangible service export with no physical office presence in Spain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered corporate domicile or virtual office lease; Spanish tax registration (Form 036/037); annual accounts filed for the SL; client contracts and e-signature logs; evidence of compliance with the EU eIDAS regulation and GDPR documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound payments from jurisdictions with high AML risk or sanctioned persons using automated contract platforms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual terms for the automation service; PEP and sanctions screening results; IP and device geolocation logs of client; invoice and payment history; transaction monitoring explanation submitted through the bank's compliance questionnaire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for shareholder capital injection uses SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's euro-denominated capital escrow account at a tier-one bank. The transfer must reference the share subscription or capital increase deed and the purpose code 'Capital contribution / Direct investment in equity.' For EU-origin transfers, the SEPA Credit Transfer may be used below the €50,000 reporting threshold. The Bank of Spain foreign direct investment declaration and the Spanish Companies Register filing must be completed simultaneously, and the receiving bank will require the notarised capital increase deed, NIE/NIF tax identifier, and source-of-funds evidence before crediting and issuing the bank confirmation certificate for the commercial registry.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for payments to international contractors, cloud infrastructure providers, and legal counsel are executed via SWIFT MT103 across the euro or foreign-currency correspondent network if the counterparty is outside SEPA. For SEPA-zone counterparties, cleared and settled SEPA Credit Transfers provide low-cost euro disbursements. Trade settlements requiring documentary security may be structured as irrevocable commercial letters of credit (LC) at sight or with deferred payment terms, opened by the Spanish bank and advised through the beneficiary's correspondent bank. All outbound payments above the balance-of-payments declaration threshold require the Bank of Spain transaction reporting form and may require applicable withholding tax evidence on royalties and software service fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot transactions for immediate conversion of EUR, USD, GBP, and other freely convertible currencies.
Deliverable FX forwards with tenor up to 3 years, available from Spanish credit institutions under MiFID II suitability controls.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted convertibility currencies where settlement is in EUR or a major convertible currency.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS / FX swaps) for managing long-term foreign-currency receivable and payable mismatches.
FX options and collars on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/LatAm currencies where permitted under applicable derivatives clearing and EMIR reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalisation of accounting books and corporate books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the financial year; generally by 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry penalties and possible evidentiary limitations; late legalisation may complicate subsequent filings. No automatic administrative strike-off solely for late book legalisation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting; minutes retained by the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the financial year; generally by 30 June for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may incur liability for breach of statutory duties. Failure to approve accounts prevents timely filing and may result in Mercantile Registry closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and management report, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; generally by 31 July for accounts approved on 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure after one year of non-deposit, preventing registration of most subsequent corporate acts; administrative fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher maximums for qualifying high-turnover companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration accompanying the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual accounts and renewed annually; changes in beneficial ownership must be reported through the applicable corporate and registry filings without delay
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate beneficial ownership information may delay or reject the accounts filing and may trigger corporate, registry, anti-money-laundering, or administrative liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, Form 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year; generally 1 to 25 July for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, late-payment interest, and potential surcharges or tax audit exposure. Repeated non-compliance may lead to enforcement proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average employees of more than 50. Additional mandatory audits apply to specified regulated, publicly funded, or otherwise legally designated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) for individual statutory accounts. IFRS applies where legally required or permitted, principally for qualifying consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and maintain current information on its ultimate beneficial owners. Beneficial ownership information is confirmed annually through the declaration accompanying the annual accounts and must be updated when ownership or control changes. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the beneficial ownership analysis.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of contracts between the sole shareholder and the company, if applicable
Beneficial ownership information and supporting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,200 per year, depending on address, mail handling, director services, and compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 1,600-6,500 for a non-complex Spanish SL; higher for regulated, multinational, or high-volume operations
